text.p: Favourites Yugoslavia got off to a good start in the European men's basketball championship with an emphatic 104-76 win over Poland on Wednesday.
The defending champions' performanchighlight of a day which brought comfortable wins for all the fancied sides.
The Yugoslavs went in at the break with only a six-point lead, but turned up the pressure to swamp the Poles in the second half.
Russia, Greece, Italy, Croatia, France, Spain and Lithuania all won their matches.
Croatia crushed 1993 winners Germany 75-55, while hosts Spain shook off doubts caused by their poor preparation games by thrashing Ukraine 82-54.
Lithuania went in at half-time a point down against Israel, but came out strongly after the break and in the end ran out easy winners 75-60.
Slovenia made France work hard, pulling level to 65-65, before succumbing 80-75, the closest result of the day.
Italy won 85-75 against Latvia, and Russia beat Bosnia 65-55.
Greece scored a convincing 74-52 over neighbours Turkey in a game which failed to produce any of the feared fireworks.
Police and other security officials nearly outnumbered spectators. None of the games, including Spain's, attracted more than 1,000 spectators.
